Exploring usability evaluation of localised software in Malaysia /

This thesis postulates the theory that software usability evaluation should be adapted to the culture in which it is carried out. An experiment has been conducted to explore the effectiveness of usability assessment tools (UATs). These UATs are studies in the context of ustability evaluation phase of the global software development life-cycle. In particular, the study investigates whether imported UATs were appropriate in the usability evaluation of a localised spreadsheet in Malaysia. The experiment reveals that there is some support for the thesis and recommends a further large-scale formal study.
Systematic studies of New Zealand nanoflagellates with special reference to members of the haptophyta /
Faculty of Research Science and Technology.

The species compositionof the nanoflagellates in New Zealand coastal waters, particularly in Blueskin Bay, was reinvestigated after 25 years. The results of this study have contributed much new information about this group of marine micro-organisms. Eighty-nine taxa, mainly from the classes Prymnesiophyceae, Chrysophyceae, Prasinophyceae, and Choanoflagellidea were postitively identified to date using both light and electron microscopy. The species number has, as a result, increased from 56 to 89. thirty-three of the documented species were new records to New Zealand, most being from the class Prymnesiophyceae. The Fact that many of the species found in New Zealand waters were also observed in northern hemisphere temperae seas strongly supports the general view that the nanomastigotes have a world-wide distribution.
